      53                         : 
      54                         : // This file implements lowering of the Slang AST to a simpler SSA
      55                         : // intermediate representation.
      56                         : //
      57                         : // IR is generated in a context (`IRGenContext`), which tracks the current
      58                         : // location in the IR where code should be emitted (e.g., what basic
      59                         : // block to add instructions to). Lowering a statement will emit some
      60                         : // number of instructions to the context, and possibly change the
      61                         : // insertion point (because of control flow).
      62                         : //
      63                         : // When lowering an expression we have a more interesting challenge, for
      64                         : // two main reasons:
      65                         : //
      66                         : // 1. There might be types that are representible in the AST, but which
      67                         : //    we don't want to support natively in the IR. An example is a `struct`
      68                         : //    type with both ordinary and resource-type members; we might want to
      69                         : //    split values with such a type into distinct values during lowering.
      70                         : //
      71                         : // 2. We need to handle the difference between l-value and r-value expressions,
      72                         : //    and in particular the fact that HLSL/Slang supports complicated sorts
      73                         : //    of l-values (e.g., `someVector.zxy` is an l-value, even though it can't
      74                         : //    be represented by a single pointer), and also allows l-values to appear
      75                         : //    in multiple contexts (not just the left-hand side of assignment, but
      76                         : //    also as an argument to match an `out` or `in out` parameter).
      77                         : //
      78                         : // Our solution to both of these problems is the same. Rather than having
      79                         : // the lowering of an expression return a single IR-level value (`IRInst*`),
      80                         : // we have it return a more complex type (`LoweredValInfo`) which can represent
      81                         : // a wider range of conceptual "values" which might correspond to multiple IR-level
      82                         : // values, and/or represent a pointer to an l-value rather than the r-value itself.
      83                         : 
      84                         : // We want to keep the representation of a `LoweringValInfo` relatively light
      85                         : // - right now it is just a single pointer plus a "tag" to distinguish the cases.
      86                         : //
      87                         : // This means that cases that can't fit in a single pointer need a heap allocation
      88                         : // to store their payload. For simplicity we represent all of these with a class
      89                         : // hierarchy:
      90                         : //
      91                         : struct ExtendedValueInfo : RefObject
      92                         : {
      93                         : };
      94                         : 
      95                         : // This case is used to indicate a value that is a reference
      96                         : // to an AST-level subscript declaration.
      97                         : //
      98                         : struct SubscriptInfo : ExtendedValueInfo
      99                         : {
     100                         :     DeclRef<SubscriptDecl> declRef;
     101                         : };
     102                         :

     104                         : // recursively contain `LoweredValInfo`s, and
     105                         : // so we forward declare them here and fill
     106                         : // them in later.
     107                         : //

     116                         : // This type is our core representation of lowered values.
     117                         : // In the simple case, it just wraps an `IRInst*`.
     118                         : // More complex cases, representing l-values or aggregate
     119                         : // values are also supported.
     120                         : struct LoweredValInfo
     121                         : {
     122                         :     typedef LoweredValInfo ThisType;
     123                         : 
     124                         :     // Which of the cases of value are we looking at?
     125                         :     enum class Flavor
     126                         :     {
     127                         :         // No value (akin to a null pointer)
     128                         :         None,
     129                         : 
     130                         :         // A simple IR value
     131                         :         Simple,
     132                         : 
     133                         :         // An l-value represented as an IR
     134                         :         // pointer to the value
     135                         :         Ptr,
     136                         : 
     137                         :         // A member declaration bound to a particular `this` value
     138                         :         BoundMember,
     139                         : 
     140                         :         // A reference to an AST-level subscript operation
     141                         :         Subscript,
     142                         : 
     143                         :         // An AST-level subscript operation bound to a particular
     144                         :         // object and arguments.
     145                         :         BoundStorage,
     146                         : 
     147                         :         // The result of applying swizzling to an l-value
     148                         :         SwizzledLValue,
     149                         : 
     150                         :         // The result of applying swizzling to an l-value matrix
     151                         :         SwizzledMatrixLValue,
     152                         : 
     153                         :         // The value extracted from an opened existential
     154                         :         ExtractedExistential,
     155                         : 
     156                         :         // The L-Value that is an implicit cast.
     157                         :         ImplicitCastedLValue
     158                         :     };

     265                         : // This case is used to indicate a reference to an AST-level
     266                         : // operation that accesses abstract storage.
     267                         : //
     268                         : // This could be an invocation of a `subscript` declaration,
     269                         : // with argument representing an index or indices:
     270                         : //
     271                         : //     RWStructuredBuffer<Foo> gBuffer;
     272                         : //     ... gBuffer[someIndex] ...
     273                         : //
     274                         : // the expression `gBuffer[someIndex]` will be lowered to
     275                         : // a value that references `RWStructureBuffer<Foo>::operator[]`
     276                         : // with arguments `(gBuffer, someIndex)`.
     277                         : //
     278                         : // This could also be an reference to a `property` declaration,
     279                         : // with no arguments:
     280                         : //
     281                         : //      struct Sphere { property radius : int { get { ... } } }
     282                         : //      Sphere sphere;
     283                         : //      ... sphere.radius ...
     284                         : //
     285                         : // the expression `sphere.radius` will be lowered to a value
     286                         : // that references `Sphere::radius` with arguments `(sphere)`.
     287                         : //
     288                         : // Such a value can be an l-value, and depending on the context
     289                         : // where it is used, can lower into a call to either the getter
     290                         : // or setter operations of the storage.
     291                         : //
     292                         : struct BoundStorageInfo : ExtendedValueInfo
     293                         : {
     294                         :     /// The declaration of the abstract storage (subscript or property)
     295                         :     DeclRef<ContainerDecl> declRef;
     296                         : 
     297                         :     /// The IR-level type of the stored value
     298                         :     IRType* type;
     299                         : 
     300                         :     /// The base value/object on which storage is being accessed
     301                         :     LoweredValInfo base;
     302                         : 
     303                         :     /// Additional arguments required to reify a reference to the storage
     304                         :     List<IRInst*> additionalArgs;
     305                         : };
